bib.title: Prefix-Tuning: Optimizing Continuous Prompts for Generation
bib.venue: Proceedings of ACL-IJCNLP 2021 (59th ACL / 11th IJCNLP), pages 4582-4597

question: Can a small continuous task-specific prefix, with the language model frozen, replace full fine-tuning for natural language generation tasks?
hypothesis: Optimizing continuous prefix activations at every layer, with the LM frozen, gives performance comparable to fine-tuning with far fewer parameters, and helps most in low-data and extrapolation settings.
contributions: Propose prefix-tuning, a lightweight alternative to fine-tuning for NLG that optimizes a continuous prefix and keeps LM parameters frozen
Apply it to GPT-2 table-to-text and BART summarization with 0.1% of the parameters
Show better low-data and unseen-topic extrapolation than fine-tuning

method.summary: A trainable matrix P_theta of |P_idx| x dim(h_i) free activations is prepended to the input (and to both encoder and decoder for BART); all LM weights are frozen and only the prefix is trained with the usual log-likelihood. P_theta is reparametrized through an MLP from a smaller matrix during training and dropped after training.
method.task: table-to-text generation (E2E, WebNLG, DART) with GPT-2; abstractive summarization (XSUM) with BART

datasets.name: E2E
datasets.preprocessing: table linearized as 'field A : value A | field B : value B'

datasets.name: WebNLG
datasets.split: 9 seen DBpedia categories in train/dev; test has seen half and 5 unseen categories (S, U, A)

datasets.name: DART
datasets.source: Radev et al., 2020 (WikiSQL, WikiTableQuestions, E2E, WebNLG, converted)

datasets.name: XSUM
datasets.split: full; low-data 50-500; extrapolation splits news-to-sports and within-news (train on world, UK, business)
datasets.preprocessing: articles truncated to 512 BPE tokens; topic identified from URL for extrapolation splits

models.name: Prefix-tuning
models.params: 250K (E2E, WebNLG), 500K (DART) vs 345M GPT-2 Medium, i.e. 0.1%; XSUM 2% and 0.1% variants
models.architecture: prefix activations P_theta (|P_idx| x dim(h_i)) via MLP from P'_theta of width k
models.init_from: random (uniform (0,1)) or activations of real words (low-data)

models.name: FT-FULL / FT-TOP2 / ADAPTER (3%, 0.1%)
models.architecture: adapter implementation same as Lin et al. (2020)

training.objective: max log p_phi(y|x) = sum over Y_idx of log p(z_i | h_<i), only prefix parameters theta trainable
training.lr: default 5e-5; searched {1e-5, 5e-5, 8e-5}; per-dataset in Table 6 (prefix: E2E 8e-5, WebNLG 5e-5, DART 5e-5, XSUM 5e-5)
training.batch_size: default 5; Table 6 prefix: E2E 10, WebNLG 5, DART 5, XSUM 14; low-data table-to-text 10; low-data summarization 5 (prefix) / 6 (fine-tune)
training.epochs: default 10; Table 6 prefix: E2E 5, WebNLG 5, DART 10, XSUM 30; search {5,10} table-to-text, {5,25,30} summarization
training.seq_len: XSUM articles truncated to 512 BPE tokens
training.regularisation: early stopping on validation (low-data; dev = 30% of training size)
training.hardware: table-to-text: TITAN Xp or GeForce GTX TITAN X; summarization: Tesla V100
training.compute: table-to-text 0.2 h/epoch on 22K examples (fine-tuning ~0.3 h); XSUM 1.25 h/epoch
training.seeds: low-data: 5 sampled datasets x 2 training seeds = 10 models per setting

other.extrapolation XSUM: within-news prefix lr 5e-5, 30 epochs, batch 36, prefix len 80; news-to-sports 5e-5, 15 epochs, batch 36, len 40
other.memory: prefix-tuning batch size 1 takes 18% of GPU memory, fine-tuning 50%
other.model selection: perplexity and automatic generation metrics on validation set; batch size = largest that fits, not tuned

inference.decoding: beam search: beam 5 table-to-text; beam 6 with length normalization 0.8 summarization
inference.samples: not stated for full-data runs (single run implied); low-data averaged over 10 models

other.decode time: 1.2 s per sentence (no batching) table-to-text; 2.6 s per batch of 10 summarization

metrics.name: BLEU, METEOR, TER, MoverScore, BERTScore, BLEURT (DART)

baselines: SOTA: Shen et al. 2019 (E2E), Kale 2020 T5-large (WebNLG)
BART fine-tuning (Lewis et al. 2020) for XSUM
eval.protocol: Test numbers in main tables; validation numbers in Tables 7, 9. No significance tests stated. Full-data runs: seed count not stated. DART SOTA unavailable.

evidence.quote: The default setting is 10 epochs, batch size 5, learning rate 5·10−5 and preﬁx length 10.

limits: Directly optimizing the prefix is unstable and sensitive to initialization (footnote 3); MLP reparametrization needed in training
Prefix-tuning underperforms fine-tuning on XSUM full data; authors hypothesize more data, longer inputs and task complexity
Why it extrapolates better is stated to be an open question
Seed counts for full-data runs, BART/GPT-2 layer counts and precision are not given
Only GPT-2 up to 774M and BART Large tested; scaling to GPT-3 is suggested not shown
Low-data and extrapolation results are small-sample averages without significance tests

terms.definition: prepends a sequence of continuous task-specific vectors (free parameters, activations at all layers) to the input, freezing the LM
class of methods optimizing a continuous prefix or prompt (prefix-tuning, p-tuning, prompt-tuning)
